Graduate School Application Information
Application procedure for the M.S. or Ph.D. in Chemistry
If you have questions at any point during your admissions process, please contact us at [email protected].
Know what to expect
Our graduate program components include:
Ph.D. program
Required coursework
Research track requirements for seminars
A preliminary oral examination
A thesis research project
Each student works with a faculty advisor in order to determine the program of courses that he or she will take after matriculation, and to undertake their research.
M.S. program
Required coursework
Research track requirements for seminars
A thesis research project (thesis M.S.) or a project report (non-thesis M.S.*)
Each student works with a faculty advisor in order to determine the program of courses that they will take after matriculation and to undertake their research
Admission deadlines
We request that applications be turned in prior to our deadline of Jan 5th, 2027, for full consideration.
GRE requirements
GRE (Graduate Record Examination) general exam scores are optional. If submitting GRE scores, OSU's code is 4586. No departmental code is required.
The Department of Chemistry recommends but does not require the submission of GRE scores.
Look at opportunities available to our grad students
Take a moment to check out our Grad Resources page to see what opportunities are available if you join our Grad Student Community!
Review our directory of faculty & contact potential mentors
Please refer to our faculty directory for the tenure-track faculty in our department. You are encouraged to contact faculty directly to get more information about their current research and to inquire whether they are accepting new graduate students in their groups.
International students
International students have additional requirements:
GRE scores are recommended but not required for all applicants
Your TOEFL or IELTS scores unless you received a greater than a B average during two terms in an accredited institution in the U.S., U.K., New Zealand, Australia or Canada
Please note the Department of Chemistry only admits new students Fall term each year.
Learn more about international admissions
Apply for graduate school at OSU
Please include the following with your application:
Your personal statement
please include your area of interest and three potential mentor(s) from our Faculty, career goals, relevant academic and research experiences, your strengths and potential challenges with strategies to overcome hurdles, and other points that are relevant for your application)
Your CV
Your transcripts
The names and contact information of three references
Any awards, posters or publications that you have
Graduate school application process
Domestic fee waiver
The Department of Chemistry at Oregon State University is pleased to offer all domestic applicants an Application Fee Waiver for the 2026-2027 academic year. Please contact [email protected] for directions on how to apply for the fee waiver within the application.
For International applicants interested in a Fee Waiver, please see below.
Apply for an International application fee waiver
Apply now for an application fee waiver (NO application fees)! If we believe that you are a good fit to our program, we will cover the application fee for you!
*Please note* that this does not guarantee admission, it is just a good gesture from the dept to encourage you to apply. Only a limited number of application fee waivers are available, so please be understanding if we cannot provide you with this kind of assistance. Whatever the outcome of the application fee waiver decision, we welcome your interest and encourage you to apply to our program.
Fee waiver application is now open! It closes Monday, Nov 30th at 5p PST
Frequently asked questions
Does the Department of Chemistry accept applications for winter or spring term?
The department only rarely accepts new graduate students in winter or spring term.
What is the recruitment season?
Recruitment season is the period of time from late September to mid March when we accept and evaluate applications and make offers.
How do I apply for an application fee waiver?
Please use this link to apply for an International fee waiver. Only PhD applicants will be considered.
Fee waiver application is now open! Closing date is Nov 30th at 5p PST
Someone will notify you of our decision. Please keep in mind only a small number of these waivers are available.
Can graduate courses completed at another university be substituted for graduate courses in chemistry at OSU?
At the discretion of the student's faculty advisor, the Department of Chemistry and the Graduate School, graduate courses taken at another university may be substituted for graduate courses in the Graduate Program in Chemistry at Oregon State University.
Is an M.S. degree required for admission into the chemistry Ph.D. program?
No.
Who will contact my references?
The Graduate School will automatically contact your references.
Can I turn in letters of recommendation that were given to me by my references?
We prefer to receive letters of recommendation via the Graduate School system.
How are applicants selected?
Once an application is complete, it is reviewed by the Graduate Recruitment Committee (GRC), which is made up of research active faculty members from each division. After the GRC has made their selections, the department will make offers to the prospective graduate students.
When should I contact someone in the department?
Here are some instances in which you should contact the department:
If you have questions about completing or turning in your application
If you have questions about the Graduate Program in Chemistry
If you have questions about Graduate Program in Chemistry events
What is the minimum TOEFL score or IELTS score necessary for admission?
The minimum required TOEFL score is an 80, with no lower than 18 in all categories except speaking, in which we require a minimum score of 22. The minimum required IELTS score is 6.5.
How recently must the TOEFL or IELTS have been taken?
These exams must be taken no more than two years before the potential start date of the applicant.
If my GPA, IELTS or TOEFL scores are below the recommended level, might I still get into the program?
In rare circumstances, applicants with scores below the requested level have been admitted into the program.
Do I need to have a prospective advisor picked out before I apply?
You should have a few different research-active faculty members in mind as potential advisors at the time that you fill out your application, but you would not officially choose an advisor until your first or second term in the program, should you be accepted.
Do I have to fill out the entire application and attach all necessary documentation before submission?
Yes.
Should I contact the faculty member or members that I would like to work with?
If you are familiar with the research of a faculty member and your interests fall in line with their own, then it may be a good idea to contact them.
Are you a GEM affiliated Institution?
YES! OSU is a GEM affiliated institution. GEM is a program that funds URM students for Graduate School. Not only does the Oregon State's College of Science participate in this program at an undergraduate level, but we also welcome all GEM applicants from OSU or other GEM institutions to apply to our Grad program!
